description: Compact coarse label vocabulary for constrained local-model cluster labeling.

labels.short_description: Broad woody or shaded forest cluster with trees, woodland herbs, or fern-rich understorey signal.
labels.use_when: Use when the topological species or first phi-ranked species point clearly toward trees, shade herbs, or woodland structure.

labels.short_description: Broad moist meadow, marsh-edge, sedge-rich, or wet graminoid-herb cluster.
labels.use_when: Use when the species core suggests wetness, sedges, marsh herbs, or moisture-tolerant graminoids.

labels.short_description: Broad dry grass-forb, calcareous meadow, or steppe-leaning open herb cluster.
labels.use_when: Use when the strongest signal comes from dry meadow, forb-grass, or steppe-like species.

labels.short_description: Mostly herbaceous cluster with a visible plant-community signal, but without a clean wet-versus-dry direction.
labels.use_when: Use when the cluster is clearly herbaceous but neither wet meadow nor dry meadow is defensible.

labels.short_description: Mixed ecotonal cluster combining signals from two directions, such as woodland-meadow or wet-dry overlap.
labels.use_when: Use when the evidence bundle shows two competing broad directions and neither clearly dominates.

labels.short_description: Broad disturbed, nitrophilous, or anthropogenic herb cluster.
labels.use_when: Use when disturbance-tolerant or ruderal herbs dominate the directional signal.

labels.short_description: Diffuse mixed cluster with weak dominance and broad generalist composition.
labels.use_when: Use when the cluster is internally real but no stronger coarse family is safer than a general mixed label.

labels.short_description: Very weakly structured mixed cluster used only as the last broad coarse label inside the constrained vocabulary.
labels.use_when: Use only if none of the other listed labels are even broadly defensible.
